evidence.quote: Maria Alvarez, who owns Alvarez Family Grocers on Union Street, was robbed at gunpoint Tuesday night as she was closing the store, according to police.
She was not physically injured, but police described her as shaken and badly frightened after the encounter.

she received a call from someone claiming to be a bank fraud investigator who convinced her that her account had been compromised and that she needed to transfer funds to a 'protected' account to keep them safe.
Alvarez reported the fraud to her bank and to local police, but said she has been told it is unlikely the funds can be recovered.

She has since partnered with a local consumer protection group to warn other small business owners about similar scams targeting people who keep irregular hours and are often distracted by running a business.
'I want people to know this can happen to anyone, no matter how careful you think you are,' Alvarez said.
Consumer protection advocates praised her willingness to share her story publicly, saying it will likely help other residents recognize the warning signs before it is too late.
